newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: IBCA assigns BB to Argentine foreign debt - gov't.
newsitem.headline: IBCA assigns BB to Argentine foreign debt - gov't.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, assigned a BB rating to Argentina's medium- and long-term foreign currency debt Thursday, Argentina's government said.
IBCA gave a B rating to Argentina's short-term foreign currency debt. The agency said the rating outlook is "positive," the Economy Ministry said in a press release.

This rating action "confirms the recent upgrade of Argentina by fellow agency Standard & Poor's and leaves the country's ratings at the same level by three of the four agencies that rate the sovereign debt," the ministry said.
S&P recently raised Argentina's foreign currency debt to BB from BB- but left the outlook at "stable."
"Since this rating is accompanied by a 'positive' outlook, it represents an additional improvement compared with the other agencies," the government added.

IBCA later confirmed the news. "There is a positive outlook for the Argentine rating, since the foundations for sustainable non-inflationary growth are in place. Indeed, Argentina is the most promising candidate for economic success in Latin America after Chile," it said in a statement.
Duff & Phelps also has Argentine long-term debt at BB while Moody's Investors Corp has it at B1.
